details:
TerraTwin – Earth to Space Analogue Explorer

TerraTwin is an interactive web-based platform designed to identify and explore Earth locations that resemble potential permanent Moon base locations and Martian environments. It helps users understand how different terrestrial landscapes can serve as analogue environments for future planetary exploration.

The platform allows users to explore Moon and Mars analogue environments, discover potential matching locations on Earth, view their geographical positions on an interactive map, and compare environmental and geographical characteristics. These include terrain, geological features, temperature conditions, elevation, and water or ice availability. The prototype includes example locations such as the Atacama Desert, McMurdo Dry Valleys, Haughton Crater, Mauna Loa, and Askja.

TerraTwin aims to make planetary analogue research more accessible and understandable. By highlighting similarities and differences between Earth and extraterrestrial environments, it can help communicate how Earth-based locations may support astronaut training, geological research, equipment testing, and preparation for future lunar and Martian missions.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Leaflet.js and OpenStreetMap for interactive geographical visualization. Predefined sample datasets are used to demonstrate location filtering, searching, and environmental comparisons. The prototype does not currently retrieve live NASA data or produce scientifically validated similarity measurements.

The creative aspect of TerraTwin lies in connecting Earth-based geographical exploration with future space exploration through a single interactive platform. Instead of presenting planetary analogue locations as isolated research information, it brings them together in a visual and comparative experience.

During development, our team considered geographical accuracy, environmental similarities, scientific limitations, accessibility of information, usability, and the feasibility of implementing the concept within the hackathon timeframe. We also considered important differences between Earth, the Moon, and Mars, including gravity, atmosphere, and radiation.

Our intended impact is to encourage interest in planetary science, support awareness of Earth-based analogue research, and demonstrate how terrestrial environments can contribute to preparing humanity for sustainable exploration beyond Earth.
